**John King** ( [Republican Party](https://ballotpedia.org/Republican_Party)) is the [Georgia Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner](https://ballotpedia.org/Georgia_Insurance_and_Safety_Fire_Commissioner). He assumed office on July 1, 2019. His current term ends on January 11, 2027.

King ( [Republican Party](https://ballotpedia.org/Republican_Party)) is running for re-election for [Georgia Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner](https://ballotpedia.org/Georgia_Insurance_and_Safety_Fire_Commissioner). He is on the ballot in the general election on [November 3, 2026](https://ballotpedia.org/Georgia_Insurance_Commissioner_election,_2026). He advanced from the Republican primary on [May 19, 2026](https://ballotpedia.org/Georgia_Insurance_Commissioner_election,_2026).

King also ran for election to the [U.S. Senate](https://ballotpedia.org/United_States_Senate) to represent Georgia. He did not appear on the ballot for the Republican primary on [May 19, 2026](https://ballotpedia.org/United_States_Senate_election_in_Georgia,_2026).

## Biography

John King earned a bachelor's degree from Brenau University and a graduate degree from the United States Army War College.
His career experience includes working in law enforcement.[\[1\]](https://ballotpedia.org/John_King_(Georgia)#cite_note-bio-1)

## Political career

### Georgia Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner (2019 - Present)

King was appointed as the insurance commissioner on June 12, 2019, after [Jim Beck](https://ballotpedia.org/Jim_Beck "Jim Beck") was suspended from the position. Beck was indicted in May 2019 on charges of wire fraud, mail fraud, and money laundering.[\[2\]](https://ballotpedia.org/John_King_(Georgia)#cite_note-2) King assumed office on July 1, 2019.[\[3\]](https://ballotpedia.org/John_King_(Georgia)#cite_note-3) As commissioner, King leads the statewide office responsible for regulating the state's insurance industry and oversees all Georgia fire safety initiatives.

##### Republican primary for U.S. Senate Georgia

[Mike Collins](https://ballotpedia.org/Mike_Collins_(Georgia)) (R) and [Derek Dooley](https://ballotpedia.org/Derek_Dooley) (R) advanced to a runoff.
